P0011.name: Intake Camshaft Position Timing - Over-Advanced (Bank 1)
P0011.description: The intake camshaft timing on Bank 1 is more advanced than the ECU commanded. Often caused by worn timing chain, faulty VVT solenoid, or low oil pressure.
commonCauses: Low engine oil level or wrong viscosity

P0012.name: Intake Camshaft Position Timing - Over-Retarded (Bank 1)
P0012.description: The intake camshaft timing on Bank 1 is more retarded than the ECU commanded. Similar causes to P0011 but timing is stuck in the retarded position.

P0014.name: Exhaust Camshaft Position Timing - Over-Advanced (Bank 1)
P0014.description: The exhaust camshaft timing is more advanced than commanded. Indicates VVT system issues on the exhaust side.

P0016.name: Crankshaft/Camshaft Position Correlation - Bank 1 Sensor A
P0016.description: The crankshaft and camshaft position sensors show a timing correlation error. The camshaft is not in the expected position relative to the crankshaft.
commonCauses: Faulty camshaft or crankshaft position sensor

P0017.name: Crankshaft/Camshaft Position Correlation - Bank 1 Sensor B
P0017.description: Similar to P0016 but for the exhaust camshaft (Sensor B). Indicates timing correlation mismatch on the exhaust side.

P0021.name: Intake Camshaft Position Timing - Over-Advanced (Bank 2)
P0021.description: Same as P0011 but for Bank 2 (opposite cylinder bank on V-engines). Intake cam timing is over-advanced.

P0022.name: Intake Camshaft Position Timing - Over-Retarded (Bank 2)
P0022.description: Same as P0012 but for Bank 2. Intake cam timing is over-retarded on the opposite bank.

P0087.name: Fuel Rail/System Pressure - Too Low
P0087.description: The fuel pressure in the rail is below the expected level. Can cause poor performance, misfires, or stalling. Common on GDI engines.

P0088.name: Fuel Rail/System Pressure - Too High
P0088.description: Fuel pressure is higher than expected. Can cause hard starting, rough idle, and potential fuel system damage.
commonCauses: Wiring issue to fuel pressure regulator

P0128.name: Coolant Thermostat Below Regulating Temperature
P0128.description: The engine is not reaching normal operating temperature within the expected time. Almost always a stuck-open thermostat.

P0171.name: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
P0171.description: The engine is running lean on Bank 1 — too much air or not enough fuel. One of the most common OBD-II codes across all makes.

P0174.name: System Too Lean (Bank 2)
P0174.description: Same lean condition as P0171 but on Bank 2. When both P0171 and P0174 appear together, the cause is typically shared (vacuum leak, MAF, or fuel delivery).

P0190.name: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0190.description: The fuel rail pressure sensor circuit is reporting abnormal readings. Can be the sensor itself or wiring.

P0191.name: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0191.description: Fuel rail pressure sensor readings are out of expected range or responding too slowly.

P0217.name: Engine Overtemperature Condition
P0217.description: The engine has exceeded the maximum allowable coolant temperature. May trigger limp mode to protect the engine.

P0230.name: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit Malfunction
P0230.description: The fuel pump primary control circuit has a malfunction. Fuel pump may not be receiving proper voltage.

P0231.name: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit - Low
P0231.description: The fuel pump secondary circuit voltage is lower than expected. Indicates the fuel pump is drawing too little current.
commonCauses: High resistance in fuel pump wiring

P0232.name: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit - High
P0232.description: The fuel pump secondary circuit voltage is higher than expected. May indicate a short circuit or relay stuck closed.

P0234.name: Turbo/Supercharger Overboost Condition
P0234.description: Boost pressure has exceeded the maximum allowable limit. Can cause engine damage if ignored. The ECU will typically cut fuel or ignition to protect the engine.

P0299.name: Turbo/Supercharger Underboost Condition
P0299.description: The turbo or supercharger is not producing the expected boost pressure. Causes noticeable loss of power.

P0300.name: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
P0300.description: The engine control module has detected misfires occurring randomly across multiple cylinders. This is the most common OBD-II code and can have many causes. A flashing check engine light with P0300 means active misfires that can damage the catalytic converter.
commonCauses: Worn spark plugs or ignition coils

P0301.name: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
P0301.description: Misfires detected specifically in cylinder 1. Unlike P0300, a single-cylinder code narrows the problem to that cylinder's ignition, fuel, or compression.
commonCauses: Low compression (worn rings or valve issue)

P0302.name: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected
P0302.description: Misfires detected specifically in cylinder 2. Same diagnostic approach as P0301 but focused on cylinder 2 components.
commonCauses: Intake manifold gasket leak near cylinder 2

P0305.name: Cylinder 5 Misfire Detected
P0305.description: Misfires detected specifically in cylinder 5. Only applies to engines with 5 or more cylinders.

P0306.name: Cylinder 6 Misfire Detected
P0306.description: Misfires detected specifically in cylinder 6. Applies to V6, I6, V8, and larger engines.

P0307.name: Cylinder 7 Misfire Detected
P0307.description: Misfires detected specifically in cylinder 7. Applies to V8 and larger engines.

P0308.name: Cylinder 8 Misfire Detected
P0308.description: Misfires detected specifically in cylinder 8. Applies to V8 and larger engines.

P0335.name: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Malfunction
P0335.description: The crankshaft position sensor circuit is not providing a valid signal. Can cause no-start or stalling conditions.

P0340.name: Camshaft Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0340.description: The camshaft position sensor is not sending a valid signal to the ECU. Can cause rough running, misfires, or no-start.

P0380.name: Glow Plug/Heater Circuit A Malfunction
P0380.description: The glow plug circuit has a malfunction. Diesel engines only. Causes hard starting in cold weather.

P0401.name: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Insufficient
P0401.description: The EGR system is not flowing enough exhaust gas back into the intake. Usually caused by carbon buildup in the EGR valve or passages.
commonCauses: Clogged EGR passages in intake manifold

P0402.name: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Excessive
P0402.description: The EGR system is flowing too much exhaust gas, causing rough idle or stalling.

P0403.name: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Circuit Malfunction
P0403.description: Electrical fault in the EGR valve control circuit. The ECU cannot properly control the EGR valve.

P0404.name: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Circuit Range/Performance
P0404.description: The EGR valve position sensor is reading outside the expected range. The valve is not moving to the commanded position.

P0420.name: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P0420.description: The catalytic converter on Bank 1 is not reducing emissions efficiently. One of the most searched OBD-II codes. Can be caused by a genuinely worn catalyst or upstream issues that damaged it.

P0430.name: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P0430.description: Same as P0420 but for the Bank 2 catalytic converter. When both P0420 and P0430 appear, the upstream cause is typically shared.

P0521.name: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch Range/Performance
P0521.description: The oil pressure sensor is reporting readings outside the expected range. Can indicate actual low oil pressure or a sensor fault.

P052E.name: Positive Crankcase Ventilation Regulator Valve Performance
P052E.description: The PCV valve is not performing correctly. Can cause oil leaks, rough idle, and increased emissions.

P0599.name: Thermostat Heater Control Circuit High
P0599.description: The electronically heated thermostat control circuit has excessive voltage. Applies to vehicles with electronically controlled thermostats.

P0671.name: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Circuit
P0671.description: Glow plug circuit fault for cylinder 1 on diesel engines.

P0700.name: Transmission Control System Malfunction
P0700.description: A generic code indicating the transmission control module (TCM) has detected a fault and set a transmission-specific code. Always appears alongside more specific transmission codes.
commonCauses: Accompanying P07xx transmission code is the real issue

P0715.name: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0715.description: The transmission input speed sensor is not sending a valid signal. Causes erratic shifting or limp mode.

P0730.name: Incorrect Gear Ratio
P0730.description: The transmission is not achieving the expected gear ratio. Usually indicates internal transmission problems like worn clutch packs or bands.

P0740.name: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Malfunction
P0740.description: The torque converter clutch solenoid circuit has a fault. Can cause poor fuel economy and transmission shudder.

P0741.name: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P0741.description: The torque converter clutch is not engaging when commanded. Causes increased fuel consumption and transmission heat.

P0742.name: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Stuck On
P0742.description: The torque converter clutch is not releasing when commanded. Can cause stalling when coming to a stop.

P0750.name: Shift Solenoid A Malfunction
P0750.description: Shift solenoid A has an electrical or performance fault. Causes harsh or no shifts.

P0751.name: Shift Solenoid A Performance/Stuck Off
P0751.description: Shift solenoid A is not engaging properly. Can cause the transmission to be stuck in one gear.

P0868.name: Transmission Fluid Pressure Low
P0868.description: Transmission fluid pressure is below the minimum threshold. Can cause slipping, harsh shifts, and transmission damage.

P189C.name: Diesel Particulate Filter Restriction - Forced Limited Power
P189C.description: The diesel particulate filter is excessively restricted, triggering forced power reduction. Common on diesel trucks.

P17F0.name: Transmission Mechanical Failure
P17F0.description: General code indicating internal mechanical transmission failure. Typically requires transmission rebuild or replacement.

P17F1.name: Transmission Gear Engagement Failure
P17F1.description: The transmission is unable to properly engage the requested gear. Often related to internal component failure.

P2181.name: Cooling System Performance
P2181.description: The cooling system is not maintaining the expected temperature range. Engine may be running too hot or too cold.

P20EE.name: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold
P20EE.description: The selective catalytic reduction system is not reducing NOx emissions effectively. Common on diesel trucks with DEF systems.

P204F.name: Reductant System Incorrect Quantity
P204F.description: The DEF (diesel exhaust fluid) injection quantity is incorrect. Part of the SCR emissions system on diesel vehicles.

P207F.name: Reductant Quality Performance
P207F.description: The DEF quality does not meet required standards. Can trigger speed limiting on diesel trucks.

P2BAF.name: NOx Exceedance - Derating Imminent
P2BAF.description: NOx emissions have exceeded limits and the vehicle will derate (limit speed/power) if not resolved. Diesel vehicles with SCR systems.
